extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding; school administrators; Title IX coordinators; institutional legal counsel; policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and interpretive guidance for determining when sex-based conduct constitutes a hostile environment under Title IX for administrative enforcement, and related procedural and First Amendment considerations for recipients of Federal education funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of hostile environment sex-based harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: The conduct must be (1) unwelcome, (2) sex-based, (3) subjectively and objectively offensive, and (4) so severe or pervasive that it results in a limitation or denial of a person's ability to participate in or benefit from the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination requires satisfaction of all listed elements. This is the Department's final definition and is intended to effectuate Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination in the administrative enforcement context. See also discussion comparing to the Davis formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjectively and objectively offensive requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Harassing conduct must be both subjectively and objectively offensive (the Department added the word 'offensive' to the subjective and objective standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The addition of 'offensive' clarifies that the complainant must perceive the conduct as offensive and that a reasonable person in the complainant's position would also find it offensive. This mirrors elements referenced in case law but is used here within the administrative enforcement definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severe or pervasive standard (administrative enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the final regulations, harassing conduct must be 'severe or pervasive' (either may suffice) rather than the Davis private-damages phrase 'severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because administrative enforcement seeks to ensure access to education (not impose monetary damages), the Department views a showing of either severity or pervasiveness as adequate to establish a hostile environment. A single serious incident—depending on circumstances—may be so severe as to create a hostile environment; pervasive conduct—even without a single severe event—may likewise create a hostile environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality of the circumstances / individualized determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether unwelcome sex-based conduct has created a hostile environment is determined based on the totality of the circumstances; a recipient must make an individualized determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should consider the ages, roles, and other relevant characteristics of the parties involved (including whether they are students or employees). The same conduct may be permissible in one context (e.g., between employees) but prohibited in another (e.g., between students or student-employee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual evaluation (ages, roles, characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must consider contextual factors such as the ages and roles of the parties and other relevant characteristics when determining whether conduct constitutes hostile environment harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors inform the objective prong of offensiveness and the totality assessment; they support making different determinations for the same conduct in different contexts (e.g., student-student vs. employee-student).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative enforcement may differ from private-damage standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department may adopt a regulatory definition for administrative enforcement that differs from the Davis/Gebser standards applied in private damages actions because administrative enforcement focuses on ensuring educational access rather than imposing monetary liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble cites Gebser and Davis as recognizing agency authority to promulgate rules for enforcement and notes prior Department guidance that used broader definitions. Courts have also allowed adapting Davis/Gebser for administrative enforcement. Thus recipients are not constrained to the private-damages formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to come into compliance / corrective measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In administrative enforcement, a recipient must be given notice and an opportunity to come into compliance before termination of funding; Department investigations generally result in agreements with recipients to take corrective measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These protective guardrails (notice, opportunity to cure, agreements for corrective action) distinguish administrative enforcement from private damages litigation and justify different standards and remedial approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedure requirements and procedural protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require recipients to adopt grievance procedures that include many procedural protections to effectuate investigations and evidence-based determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of required protections discussed include equitable treatment of parties, an equal opportunity to access relevant evidence, and the objective evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence prior to determination. These procedures are intended to ensure a fair process for all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment conformity (§106.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Title IX regulations requires a recipient to restrict any rights that would otherwise be protected from government action by the First Amendment; recipients must formulate, interpret, and apply rules in a manner that respects legal rights of students and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes that the final definition is sufficiently closely aligned with Davis for First Amendment concerns, and reiterates §106.6(d) as a backstop ensuring recipients should not impose discipline or policies that conflict with constitutional protections. Recipients must avoid infringing on academic freedom, religious liberty, freedom of association, or protected speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding overbreadth and chilling effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulators and recipients must be mindful that broad application could chill protected speech (e.g., classroom discussion, controversial research, or campus debate), and commenters raised concerns about reporting/tracking requirements leading to investigations that chill speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department responds that the final definition does not infringe constitutional rights and that grievance procedures and §106.6(d) help prevent overreach; recipients should calibrate reporting and enforcement practices to avoid unnecessary chill while addressing harassment that limits educational access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Title VII principles where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The final definition aligns closely with Title VII hostile-environment sexual harassment definitions in many respects but is crafted specifically for education programs and activities governed by Title IX rather than simply adopting Title VII wholesale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment provides administrative and compliance benefits because many recipients must comply with both Title VII and Title IX. Nevertheless, the Department tailored the definition for educational contexts and for administrative enforcement goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary action vs. damages liability
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may impose disciplinary action against a respondent for violating its policies regardless of whether the recipient would be liable for monetary damages in private action; absence of damages liability does not immunize respondents from discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department sees no logical inconsistency in permitting discipline even where private damages liability would not attach; administrative enforcement aims to secure compliance and educational access through corrective and disciplinary measures as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of special contexts (speech on abortion, religion, association)
rubrics_metrics.description: When harassment allegations intersect with contested areas like abortion advocacy/opposition, religious exercise, or freedom of association, recipients must ensure enforcement does not compel endorsement or suppression of sincerely held beliefs or unlawfully impinge associational rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department acknowledges commenters' concerns and reiterates that rules should be applied with respect for constitutional protections and applicable state laws that may extend speech protections to private institutions.
